BAD CREEK PUMPED STORAGE PROJECT EROSION AND SEDIMENT POLLUTION CONTROL PLAN
1. INTRODUCTION
This plan sets forth principles and procedures for use in erosion and sediment pollution control during construction of the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project.
2. SITE LOCATION
The Bad Creek Project site is located in Oconee County, South Carolina approximately 22 miles north of Seneca, South Carolina. The site is immediately east-southeast of the intersection of County Roads 171 and 413.
3. SITE OWNERSHIP
All construction activities are to be conducted on land owned by Duke Power Company. Completed facilities will be owned, operated, and maintained by Duke Power Company.
4. SURFACE WATERS TO BE PROTECTED
This plan is to protect surface waters from sediment pollution because of construction activities. These waters include:
1. Howard Creek from Lake Jocassee to the confluence of Howard Creek and an unnamed tributary running parallel to County Road 171. The tributary is just west of the road.
2. The Whitewater River from the North Carolina  South Carolina State boundary to Lake Jocassee.
3. The Whitewater arm of Lake Jocassee.
Bad Creek and West Bad Creek will be initially impounded to form sediment basins and finally impounded by the Main Dam and West Dam respectfully. Therefore, these creeks will be protected from sediment pollution below the impoundments.
5. SITE SOIL CHARACTERISTICS
The Bad Creek site is located in the Blue Ridge physiographic and geologic provinces. The bedrock mainly consists of granitic gneiss (Toxaway Gneiss). However, in the West Bad Creek area, the bedrock is schist. Soils in the project area are residual from in-place weathering of bedrock. The soils consist of sandy-silts (Unified Classification SM-ML) at the surface and silty-sands (SM) just below the surface.
